name: Sleep
rangeNote: Adults are advised to sleep at least 7 hours a night regularly: 7–9 hours suits most adults, 7–8 from 65. The range is checked against your average over the last week, never one night: one short night isn't a problem. More than 9 can be right for young adults, after sleep loss or during illness. Wearables measure sleep less exactly than a sleep lab. Counted per night and dated by the morning you woke up; naps on the same day are added.
summary: Time actually asleep in a night, from a watch, ring, phone app or your own note. Not time in bed: lying awake doesn't count.

high.meaning: Long sleep is usually fine. Regularly needing much more than 9 hours, or still feeling tired after it, is worth mentioning to a doctor.

low.meaning: Regularly sleeping less than 7 hours is linked to worse mood, concentration, blood sugar and blood pressure over time. Ongoing trouble sleeping or loud snoring with pauses in breathing is worth discussing with a doctor.
